ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p21/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p21/r5.speaker: Some exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p21/r5.claim: A common interpretation is that the Prophet’s daytime responsibilities leave little time for concentrated prayer, making tahajjud especially necessary.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p21/r5.anchor: Generally people are of the opinion that this verse tells the Prophet (sws) that he has a lot of other work to do during the day

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r1.claim: Islahi rejects the common reading that daytime busyness explains the verse: the night is inherently suited to prayer; sabḥ rarely means being busy without contextual evidence, and tawīlan fits the sense of glorification better than busyness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r1.anchor: For these reasons, I am unable to convince myself of the conventional interpretation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r2.claim: The verse calls for daytime glorification as well as night prayer; the Prophet remembered God in daily activities, and transmitted supplications can turn ordinary routines into worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p22/r2.anchor: the meaning of the verse is that besides the tahajjud prayer which the Prophet must offer at night, during the day also he has a lot of time for glorifying the Almighty

QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r5.claim: Daytime offers many occupations and journeys, while night leaves the Prophet freer for worship.
QUSHAYRI:v3p360/r5.anchor: فالمعنى : مذاهبك في النهار فيما يشغلك كثيرة - والليل أخلى لك

NAHHAS:v5p57/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p57/r1.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
NAHHAS:v5p57/r1.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar reads sabkhan with khāʾ, meaning relief and sleep; the report's tusabkhī means easing.
NAHHAS:v5p57/r1.anchor: وعن يحيى بن يعمر أنه قرأ ( سبخا ) بخاء معجمة أي راحة ونوما

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r15.claim: One reading of the long daytime activity is that worldly movement and duties obstruct the quiet and concentration available at night.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r15.anchor: Yeryüzünde hareket, meşgul edecek, kıraat ve ibadete mâni‘işler vardır.

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r16.claim: A second reading is that daytime is a suitable time to attend to other needs and important tasks.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r16.anchor: diğer havâyicini ve mühim işlerini görecek müsâid bir zaman vardır

ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r17.claim: A third, future-oriented reading offers glad tidings that after the commanded night vigil the Prophet will attain a long period of purification; the author compares the dawn image with 74:34.
ELMALILI:73:2-19#2/r17.anchor: Bu kıyam ile me’mur olduğun gecenin bir gündüzü gelecektir ki sen o zaman uzun bir nezâhete ve temizliğe ereceksin

ABUDAWUD:1304/r4.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:1304/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUDAWUD:1304/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the long daytime “sabh” as a long period of free time.
ABUDAWUD:1304/r4.anchor: وَقَوْلُهُ ‏{‏ إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلاً ‏}‏ يَقُولُ فَرَاغًا طَوِيلاً

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r1.claim: The common سبحا is a verbal noun from سبح, metaphorically likening daytime activity in one's affairs to swimming far through water.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r1.anchor: وهو مصدر سبح، وهو استعارة، استعار للتصرف في الحوائج السباحة في الماء

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mur, Ikrima, and Ibn Abi Abla read سبخا with خ instead of ح.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r2.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وعكرمة وابن أبي عبلة سبخا " بالخاء المعجمة

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains سبخا as teased wool spreading its parts, a metaphor for worries dispersing the heart.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r3.anchor: استعارة من سبخ الصوف: وهو نفشه ونشر أجزائه لانتشار الهم وتفرق القلب

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r4.claim: A second sense of سبخ is easing or relieving; al-Asma'i uses سبخ الله عنك الحمى for easing someone's fever.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r4.anchor: حكى الأصمعي: سبخ الله عنك الحمى، أي: خففها عنك

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r5.claim: A poet uses سبخ to mean relieve, and لا تسبخي بدعائك means do not make your supplication weaker.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r5.anchor: فسبخ عليك الهم واعلم بأنه إذا قدر الرحمن شيئا فكائن

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r6.claim: Another sense is stretching: سبخي قطنك means stretch your cotton; سبيخة is a cotton piece, plural سبائخ.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r6.anchor: وقيل: التسبيخ: المد. يقال: سبخي قطنك، أي: مديه، والسبيخة: قطعة من القطن

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r7.speaker: الأخطل
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r7.claim: Al-Akhtal's line about cotton tufts documents the plural سبائخ.

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r8.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r8.claim: Al-Razi says Ibn Ya'mur and Ikrima interpreted سبخا as daytime sleep to help with night prayer, and says their explanation should bound interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الفضل الرازي: " وقرأ ابن يعمر وعكرمة " سبخا " بالخاء معجمة وقالا: معناه نوما

SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r9.claim: Al-Samin objects that the readers transmitted a reading and offered an interpretation, which does not rule out other explanations of the word.
SAMIN-DURR:73:7/r9.anchor: ولا يلزم من ذلك أنه لا يجوز غير ما ذكرا من تفسير اللفظة

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r5.claim: The day provides a long period of free time and activity.

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r6.claim: The preferred reading is sabḥan with ḥāʾ; sabkhan with khāʾ is sound Arabic and gives a similar sense of ample scope.

ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r7.claim: Sabkhan can mean a tuft of cotton; sabakhtu cotton means to fluff it, suggesting expansion and ample daytime scope.
ZAJJAJ:v5p240/r7.anchor: يقال للقطعة من القطن سبخة، ويقال سبخت القطن بمعنى نفشته، ومعنى نفشته وسعته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r1.claim: The cited hadith uses sabakh in supplication; lexical evidence explains the word through lightening, extending, or spreading, including teased cotton.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r2.claim: Al-Asma'i says sabbakha Allah ʿanka al-humm means God lightened your fever; sabakh can also mean stretching, as in stretching cotton.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r2.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: يقال سبخ الله عنك الحمى، أي خففها. وقيل: السبخ: المد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r3.speaker: الأخطل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r3.claim: Al-Akhtal's line uses sabā'ikh for teased cotton, the singular being sabīkha.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p315/r3.anchor: سبائخ، الواحدة سبيخة، ومنه قول الأخطل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.claim: Sabh means extensive movement among daytime duties and concerns, which prevents full devotion to worship; the word originally means swift movement through water, then movement generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.anchor: أي تقلبا وتصرفا من مهماتك واشتغالا بشواغلك فلا تستطيع أن تتفرع للعبادة فعليك بها في الليل وأصل السبح المر السريع في الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.claim: The verse gives the external motive for night prayer, following the account of its internal motive.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.anchor: وهذا بيان للداعي الخارجي إلى قيام الليل بعد بيان ما في نفسه من الداعي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.claim: One alternative takes sabh as daytime leisure and spaciousness for sleep and attending to one's needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.anchor: وقيل أي أن لك في النهار فراغا وسعة لنومك وتصرفك في حوائجك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.claim: Another alternative says missed night worship can be made up during free daytime hours; sabh can mean free time.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.anchor: وقيل إن فاتك من الليل شيء فلك في النهار فراغ تقدر على تداركه فيه فالسبح لفراغ

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.claim: The first interpretation better fits the original sense of swimming or movement and the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.anchor: لكن الأول أوفق لمعنى قولهم سبح في الماء وأنسب للمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r6.claim: On the free-time reading, the verse either completes the rationale for night worship because daytime allows rest, or urges preserving the vigil since it must be made up by day.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r6.anchor: إما تتميم للعلة يهون عليه أن النهار يصلح للإستراحة فليغنم الليل للعبادة وليشكر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r7.claim: The make-up interpretation subtly evokes the alternation of night and day described in 25:62.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r7.anchor: وفيه تلويح إلى معنى جعل الليل والنهار خلفة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r8.speaker: ابن يعمر وعكرمة وابن أبيعبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r8.claim: Ibn Yaʿmar, ʿIkrima, and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read sabkhan with khāʾ; one sense is a heart scattered among worldly concerns, likened to teasing wool apart.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن يعمر وعكرمة وابن أبيعبلة سبخا بالخاء المعجمة أي تفرق قلب بالشواغل مستعار من سبخ الصوف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r9.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r9.claim: Many explain the variant as relief from obligations; al-Asmaʿi says sabbakha Allah fever means God eased it, and a report uses it for lessening a supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r9.anchor: وقال غير واحد خفة من التكاليف قال الأصمعي يقال سبخ الله تعالى عنك الحمى خففها وفي الحديث لا تسبخي بدعائك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r10.claim: A further lexical sense is stretching: the verb can mean stretch cotton, and pieces of teased cotton are called sabāʾikh.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r10.anchor: وقيل السبخ المد يقال سبخي قطنك أي مديه ويقال لقطع القطن سبائخ الواحدة سبخة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r11.speaker: الأخطل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r11.claim: Al-Akhtal's verse compares hunters scattering dust to teased cotton, illustrating sabāʾikh.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r11.anchor: ومنه قول الأخطل يصف قناصا وكلابا فأرسلوهن يذرين التراب كما يذري سبائخ قطن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r12.speaker: ابن يعمر وعكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r12.claim: The Lawāmiʿ says Ibn Yaʿmar and ʿIkrima read the variant and explained it as daytime sleep to help night prayer; the author treats sleep as an implied consequence rather than the direct meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p105#2/r12.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح أن ابن يعمر وعكرمة فسرا سبخا بالمعجمة بعد أن قرآ به فقالا معناه نوما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r1.claim: Sabh is movement in errands and work; its root is swift going, as in swimming.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r1.anchor: أي: تصرفا وتقلبا وإقبالا وإدبارا في حوائجك وأشغالك، وأصل "السبح" سرعة الذهاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r2.claim: Another view takes this as daytime room for sleep and needs, leaving prayer for night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: "سبحا طويلا" أي: فراغا وسعة لنومك وتصرفك في حوائجك فصل من الليل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r3.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar reads sabkhan with khāʾ, meaning bodily rest and lightness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر "سبخا" بالخاء المعجمة أي: استراحة وتخفيفا للبدن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r4.claim: The Prophet told ʿĀʾishah not to lighten a thief's case through prayer against him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p254#2/r4.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة، وقد دعت على سارق: "لا تسبخي عنه بدعائك عليه"

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r1.claim: The day brings prolonged movement among duties, so the Prophet should keep night vigil because intimate communion with God requires free time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r1.anchor: تقلبا في مهماتك واشتغالا بها فعليك بالتهجد، فإن مناجاة الحق تستدعي فراغا

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r2.claim: A reading has sabkhan, meaning a heart scattered by distractions, metaphorically from carding and spreading wool fibers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:7-9/r2.anchor: أي تفرق قلب بالشواغل مستعار من سبخ الصوف وهو نقشه ونشر أجزائه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r10.claim: Night worship is paired with daytime livelihood: earning provision supports religious duties and dependents without laziness, weariness, or excess.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r10.anchor: مبينا ما به صلاح الدنيا التي هي فيها المعاش

BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r11.claim: The address may be to any night worshipper or specifically the Prophet; addressing him would strengthen the obligation for the community.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p206/r11.anchor: أي أيها المتهجد أو يا أكرم العباد غن كان الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليكون آكد في إلزام الأمة به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r1.claim: Daytime activity is extended movement and turning about; a diligent person seems to swim freely through unobstructed space.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r1.anchor: حتى يكون كأنه لشدة عزمه وسرعة حركته كالسابح فيما لا عائق له فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r2.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r2.claim: Al-Baghawi says the root sense of sabḥ is going quickly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r2.anchor: قال البغوي : وأصل السبح سرعة الذهاب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r3.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p207/r3.claim: Al-Razi explains sabḥ as ease of movement.

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses daytime as distraction and movement among affairs.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأقوم قيلا} قال: أدنى من أن يفقه القرآن وفي قوله: {إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا} قال: فزاغا

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r7.claim: The daytime respite is free time for one's needs and sleep.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا} قال: السبح الفراغ للحاجة والنوم

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r8.claim: Mujahid defines the daytime respite as free time.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {سبحا طويلا} قال: فراغا

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r9.speaker: أبو مالك والربيع
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r9.claim: Abu Malik and al-Rabiʿ give the same gloss: free time.

DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.claim: Qatada defines daytime as a long free span and devotion as giving God supplication and worship exclusively.
DURR-FULL:v8p317/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {سبحا طويلا} قال: فراغا طويلا {وتبتل إليه تبتيلا} قال: أخلص له الدعوة والعبادة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says sabh includes various kinds of activity for one's needs and sleep.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3380#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : السبح انواع للحاجة والنوم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.claim: ʿIkrima reads “wrapped up” metaphorically as taking on the prophetic mission: expend effort in conveying it by night and day, except necessary sleep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة : معناه زملت هذا الأمر فقم به ، يريد أمر النبوءة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r3.claim: If al-Muzzammil preceded al-Muddaththir, revelation began with 96:1, then answered the accusation of madness prompted by al-Walid, soothed the Prophet after the slander, and later resumed with al-Muddaththir after he saw the angel at Hira.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r3.anchor: فإذا كانت سورة المزمل قد أنزلت قبل سورة المدثر كان ذلك دالا على أن الله تعالى بعد أن ابتدأ رسوله بالوحي بصدر سورة { اقرأ باسم ربك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r12.claim: The uncoordinated sentence does not specify daytime prayers, since the five prayers were not yet prescribed according to the common view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r12.anchor: فصل هذه الجملة دون عطف على ما قبلها يقتضي أن مضمونها ليس من جنس حكم ما قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r13.claim: One possibility is that the day verse explains why night was chosen: its prayer has deeper effect and firmer recitation, while daytime work leaves no solitude for the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r13.anchor: لأن النهار زمن فيه شغل عظيم لا يترك لك خلوة بنفسك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r14.claim: Alternatively, the verse gently justifies the night-prayer burden by allowing daytime rest after fatigue and time for the Prophet's daytime responsibilities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p263/r14.anchor: وفيه إرشاد إلى أن النهار ظرف واسع لإيقاع ما عسى أن يكلفه فيام الليل من فتور بالنهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r13.claim: سبحا طويلا means extensive daytime activity and movement through one's affairs, like a swimmer moving in water; a horse is also called سابح for its flexing and motion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r13.anchor: أي تصرفا وترددا في أمورك كما يتردد السابح في الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r14.speaker: قوم من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r14.claim: Some scholars take the verse to mean that if sleep or an excuse causes one to miss the night's portion, one should make it up by day, when there is ample time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r14.anchor: وقال قوم من أهل العلم إنما معنى الآية التنبيه على أنه إن فات حزب الليل بنوم أو عذر فليخلف بالنهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r15.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r15.claim: They read سبخا with dotted khāʾ; it means relief from obligations, since tasbīkh means lightening.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r15.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وعكرمة: «سبخا طويلا» بالخاء منقوطة، ومعناه خفة لك من التكاليف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r16.claim: The Prophet told Aisha not to lighten matters for the thief who stole from her, illustrating the sense of تسبيخ as easing or lessening.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r16.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ولا تسبخي عنه» لعائشة في السارق الذي سرقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r17.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r17.claim: Abu Hatim says Yahya interpreted the word سبح as sleep.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#3/r17.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: فسر يحيى السبح بالنوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ata say the day gives you ample free time for sleep and rest, so devote the night’s new hours to worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r1.anchor: أي فراغا لنومك وراحتك فاجعل ناشئة الليل لعبادتك قاله ابن عباس وعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وأبو عمران وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r2.claim: These readers use sabkhan with khāʾ; al-Zajjaj says it conveys spaciousness, from the sense of loosening or fluffing cotton.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p392/r2.anchor: وقرأ علي وابن مسعود وابو عمران وابن أبي عبلة سبخا بالخاء المعجمة قال الزجاج ومعناها في اللغة صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وعطاء بن أبي مسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r8.claim: They explain the long daytime span as free time and sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وعطاء بن أبي مسلم: الفراغ والنوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r9.speaker: أبو العالية، ومجاهد، وابن مالك، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وسفيان الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r9.claim: These authorities explain سبحا طويلا as a long period of free time.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو العالية، ومجاهد، وابن مالك، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وسفيان الثوري: فراغا طويلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r10.claim: Qatada expands the meaning to free time, pursuit of needs, and movement from place to place.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r11.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the phrase as abundant voluntary worship.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says attend to daytime needs and devote the night to religion; this applied when night prayer was obligatory, before 73:20 eased it, and Ibn Kathir endorses his account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p251#2/r12.anchor: قال: لحوائجك، فأفرغ لدينك الليل. قال: وهذا حين كانت صلاة الليل فريضة

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r13.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r13.claim: The common reading سبحا with ḥāʾ means free, spacious time for daytime affairs; its root also refers to swift movement, swimming, and a fast horse.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r13.anchor: قراءة العامة: سبحا بالحاء غير معجمة، أي: فراغا وسعة لتصرفك في حوائجك

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r14.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r14.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mar reads سبخا with khāʾ for relief or rest; a report from Aisha cites the Prophet using the related verb for easing, and the root can mean loosening or fluffing fiber.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r14.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر: سبخا بالخاء المعجمة، أراد: خفة واستراحة

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r15.speaker: ثعلب
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r15.claim: Tha'lab contrasts سبح as movement and agitation with سبخ as rest or stillness, citing the report to cool or ease a fever.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r15.anchor: قال ثعلب: السبح: التردد والاضطراب. والسبخ: السكون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r1.claim: Sabḥan with sīn means activity and movement among tasks and needs, leaving the night free for intimate converse with God, which requires an unoccupied mind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r1.anchor: تصرفا وتقلبا في مهماتك وشواغلك ، ولا تفرغ إلا بالليل ؛ فعليك بمناجاة الله التي تقتض فراغ البال وانتفاء الشواغل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r2.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r2.claim: A reading with khāʾ instead of sīn is a metaphor from teasing apart wool fibers, like the scattering of concern and the heart through distractions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r2.anchor: وأما القراءة بالخاء فاستعارة من سبخ الصوف ، وهو نفشه ونشر أجزائه ؛ لانتشار الهم وتفرق القلب بالشواغل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r3.claim: Night is more conducive to inner agreement and recitation because people are calm and quiet; it gathers the heart and concerns, unlike daytime distractions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r3.anchor: وهو أن الليل أعون على المواطأة وأشد للقراءة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r4.claim: Another view takes sabḥan as free time and spaciousness for sleep and tending to one's needs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : فراغا وسعة لنومك وتصرفك في حوائجك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r5.claim: Another view says missed night prayer can be made up in free time during the day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p640#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن فاتك من الليل شيء فلك في النهار فراغ تقدر على تداركه فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r26.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r26.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAta say the day gives ample time for sleep and rest, leaving night for worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r26.anchor: يعني فراغا طويا لنومك وراحتك , فاجعل ناشئة الليل لعبادتك , قاله ابن عباس وعطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r27.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r27.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd take sabḥ as abundant supplication; in Arab usage the word also means going or traveling, as a swimmer moves through water.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p126/r27.anchor: دعاء كثيرا , قاله السدي وابن زيد والسبح بكلامهم هو الذهاب , ومنه سبح السابح في الماء

BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r9.claim: Sabh means movement and activity through the day's concerns, like a swimmer's motion in water; daytime occupations keep the Prophet from devoting himself to worship.
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r9.anchor: أي تقلبا وتصرفا في مهما تك كتردد السابح

BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r10.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r10.claim: Al-Raghib defines sabh as rapid movement through water or air, extended to stars moving in their orbits, horses running, and rapid work.
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r10.anchor: قال الراغب : السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء

BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r11.claim: The related Qur'anic usages are the heavenly bodies swimming in their orbits and the runners moving swiftly.
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r11.anchor: كقوله تعالى وكل في فلك يسبحون ولجري الفرسك قوله تعالى فالسابحات سبحا

BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r12.speaker: تاج المصادر
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r12.claim: Taj al-Masadir glosses sabh as managing or moving about in one's livelihood.
BURSEVI:v10p161#2/r12.anchor: وفي تاج المصادر السبح تصرف كردن در معيشت

BURSEVI:v10p162/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r1.speaker: بعض التفاسير
BURSEVI:v10p162/r1.claim: Some commentaries explain sabh through the movement of hands and feet while swimming.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r1.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير قيل السباحة لما فيها من التقلب باليد والرجل في الماء

BURSEVI:v10p162/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r2.speaker: بعض التفاسير
BURSEVI:v10p162/r2.claim: Another explanation says that if a little night prayer is missed, the Prophet has daytime free time to make it up, so his communion with God is not diminished.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r2.anchor: وقيل معنى الآية إن فإنك من الليل شيء فلك في النهار فراغ تقدر على تداركه فيه حتى لا ينقص شيء من حظك

BURSEVI:v10p162/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r3.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p162/r3.claim: The Prophet says whoever sleeps through his regular night portion, or part of it, and recites it between dawn prayer and noon receives the reward as if he read it at night.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r3.anchor: قوله عليه السلام من نام عن حزبه أو عن شيء منه فقرأه

BURSEVI:v10p162/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r4.speaker: بعض المشايخ
BURSEVI:v10p162/r4.claim: Some shaykhs advise a sincere disciple to restore a missed regular devotion, even after a month, so the self does not become accustomed to laziness; regular litanies follow the Prophet and exemplary community.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r4.anchor: ومن أقوال المشايخ إن المريد الصادق إذا فاته ورد من أوراده يليق به أن يقضيه ولو بعد شهر

BURSEVI:v10p162/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p162/r5.speaker: صاحب قوت القلوب
BURSEVI:v10p162/r5.claim: Qut al-qulub says a missed voluntary wird is not legally made up like an obligatory prayer; do an equivalent when remembered as discipline and training in resolve, lest the soul get used to concessions.
BURSEVI:v10p162/r5.anchor: وفي قوت القلوب من فاته ورد من الأوردا استحب له فعل مثله متى ذكره لا على وجه القضاء لأنه لا تقضي إلا الفرائض

MUQATIL:73:7-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r1.claim: The long daytime interval is free time for sleep and other needs; they prayed only at night, which became difficult for some.
MUQATIL:73:7-11/r1.anchor: { إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا } [آية: 7] يعني فراغا طويلا لنومك ولحاجتك، وكانوا لا يصلون إلا بالليل، حتى أنه كان الرجل يعلق نفسه بالليل، فشق القيام عليه بالليل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p291/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291/r1.claim: Sabḥan means the day's extended movement among tasks and concerns, or a long period of free time for sleep and rest.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p291/r1.anchor: تصرفا وتقلبا في مهماتك وشواغلك ففرغ نفسك في الليل لعبادة ربك أو فراغا طويلا لنومك وراحتك

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r1.claim: The common reading sabḥan with ḥāʾ means daytime activity in one’s needs, going back and forth; sabḥ denotes running or circling, like a swimmer or a fast-running horse, as in Imruʾ al-Qays’s cited line.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة بالحاء غير معجمة أي تصرفا في حوائجك، وإقبالا وإدبارا وذهابا ومجيئا.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r2.claim: Other explanations of sabḥan are free time for daytime needs, sleep, or stretching; al-Khalīl records stretching as the sense of tasabbuḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: السبح الفراغ أي إن لك فراغا للحاجات بالنهار. وقيل: { إن لك في النهار سبحا } أي نوما، والتسبح التمدد

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ take the phrase as ample daytime time for sleep and rest, leaving night prayer for worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وعطاء: «سبحا طويلا» يعني فراغا طويلا لنومك وراحتك،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says daytime gives time to make up anything missed during the night.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إن فاتك في الليل شيء فلك في النهار فراغ الاستدراك.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r5.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وأبو وائل
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r5.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Abū Wāʾil read sabkhan with khāʾ; al-Mahdawī says this reading means sleep, while other glosses include ease, spaciousness, and relief.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وأبو وائل «سبخا» بالخاء المعجمة. قال المهدوي: ومعناه النوم

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r1.claim: When ʿĀʾisha cursed a thief who took her cloak, the Prophet told her not to lighten the thief’s burden with her invocation; the phrase illustrates relief from sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r1.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة وقد دعت على سارق ردائها: «لا تسبخي عنه بدعائك عليه»

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r2.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says sabbakha can mean that God removes fever or that heat abates; tasbīkh also means deep sleep.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r2.anchor: الأصمعي: يقال سبخ الله عنك الحمى أي خففها.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r3.claim: The root also describes fluffing cotton, flax, or wool; sabīkha is a tuft after carding, as illustrated by al-Akhṭal’s line about cotton tufts.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r3.anchor: والتسبيخ أيضا توسيع القطن والكتان والصوف وتنفيشها يقال للمرأة: سبخي قطنك.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r4.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r4.claim: Thaʿlab says sabkh with khāʾ can mean agitation or stillness; the Prophetic instruction to cool fever means to calm it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r4.anchor: وقال ثعلب: السبخ بالخاء التردد والاضطراب، والسبخ أيضا السكون ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr glosses sabkh as sleep or free time; al-Qurṭubī says it is then an antonym and synonymous in sense with sabḥ using ḥāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:6-7#4/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: السبخ: النوم والفراغ. قلت: فعلى هذا يكون من الأضداد، وتكون بمعنى السبح، بالحاء غير المعجمة.

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r1.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says sabḥ means movement and turning through necessary tasks; a swimmer is called sābiḥ because hands and feet move.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r1.anchor: قال المبرد : سبحا أي تقلبا فيما يجب

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that daytime brings many activities and duties, leaving the Prophet free for God's service only at night, hence the night-prayer command.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r2.anchor: إن لك في النهار تصرفا وتقلبا في مهماتك فلا تتفرغ لخدمة الله إلا بالليل

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says any sleep or rest missed at night can be made up in the day's free time.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : أي إن فاتك من الليل شيء من النوم

RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r4.claim: A variant reads sabkhan with khāʾ; it metaphorically evokes wool teased and spread out, like a heart dispersed by daytime distractions and shifting concerns.
RAZI-FULL:v30p156#2/r4.anchor: وهو استعارة من سبخ الصوف وهو نفشه ونشر أجزائه

STUDYQURAN:73:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:7/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:73:7/r1.claim: “Lengthy affairs” means daytime responsibilities that leave no time for extensive devotion.
STUDYQURAN:73:7/r1.anchor: Lengthy affairs refers to the responsibilities that prevent one from having time for extensive devotions during the day (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:73:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:7/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:73:7/r2.claim: Alternatively, God grants an extensive span for worldly matters, implying that a part of the night should be devoted to prayer.
STUDYQURAN:73:7/r2.anchor: or to God’s granting an extensive expanse of time for worldly matters, thus implying the responsibility to devote a part of the night to prayer (IK).

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r1.claim: The day gives Muhammad and his community a long span of room for their needs and activity.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r1.anchor: وإنما عني بقوله: {إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا} [المزمل: 7] إن لك في النهار سعة لقضاء حوائجك وقومك

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the long daytime respite as free time, meaning sleep.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {سبحا طويلا} [المزمل: 7] فراغا طويلا، يعني النوم

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses it as a long enjoyment or means of use.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا} [المزمل: 7] قال: متاعا طويلا

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r4.claim: Qatada says it means a long free span.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {سبحا طويلا} [المزمل: 7] قال: فراغا طويلا

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the day is for one's needs, so one should devote the night to religion.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا} [المزمل: 7] قال: لحوائجك، فافرغ لدينك الليل

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r7.speaker: أبو معاذ
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r7.claim: Abu Muadh also explains the phrase as a long free span.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r7.anchor: قال: سمعت أبا معاذ، يقول في قوله: {إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا} [المزمل: 7] فراغا طويلا

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r8.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r8.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar read the word with khāʾ as sabkhan, and this variant was explained as sleep.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r8.anchor: عن يحيى بن يعمر، من جذيلة قيس أنه كان يقرأ: «سبخا طويلا» قال: وهو النوم

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r9.claim: Al-Tabari explains tasbikh as loosening and fluffing cotton or wool; al-Akhtal's line about cotton fluff spread by combers illustrates the usage.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: والتسبيخ: توسيع القطن والصوف وتنفيشه، يقال للمرأة: سبخي قطنك

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r10.claim: Al-Tabari says sabh and sabkh are close in sense here, both conveying ample daytime room for needs.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r10.anchor: والسبح والسبخ قريبا المعنى في هذا الموضع

SULAMI:v2p355#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p355#5/r1.speaker: ابن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p355#5/r1.claim: Ibn Tahir interprets the long daytime activity as service, turning toward God, and waiting for the arrivals of revelation.
SULAMI:v2p355#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن طاهر : أشتغالا بالخدمة وإقبالا على الله وانتظارا لموارد الوحي .

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r8.claim: Sabhan means swimming swiftly in water; a long swim by day figuratively describes immersion in livelihood concerns and varied errands.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r8.anchor: السبح المشي السريع في الماء والسبح الطويل في النهار كناية عن الغور في مهمات المعاش

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r9.claim: The day is filled with many consuming occupations, leaving no free time for complete orientation toward God; therefore the Prophet should pray at night.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r9.anchor: إن لك في النهار مشاغل كثيرة تشتغل بها مستوعبة لا تدع لك فراغا

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r10.claim: Another view says daytime affords time to sleep, manage livelihood, and attend to needs, leaving the night for vigil.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r10.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن لك في النهار فراغا لنومك وتدبير أمر معاشك والتصرف في حوائجك

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r11.claim: A further view says missed night worship can be made up in the day, as in 25:62.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r11.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن لك في النهار فراغا فإن فاتك من الليل شيء أمكنك أن تتداركه في النهار

TABATABAI:73:7-8/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r12.claim: The interpretation of daytime as consuming work best fits the context; the make-up interpretation is linked to 25:62.
TABATABAI:73:7-8/r12.anchor: والذي قدمناه من المعنى أنسب للمقام

TABRISI:73:1-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10/r7.claim: Sabḥ means movement or turning about, like a swimmer moving through water.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r7.anchor: والسبح التقلب ومنه السابح في الماء لتقلبه فيه

TABRISI:73:1-10/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r8.speaker: يحيى ابن يعمر والضحاك
TABRISI:73:1-10/r8.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read sabkhan with khāʾ, meaning expansion or spreading.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r8.anchor: وقرأ يحيى ابن يعمر والضحاك سبخا طويلا بالخاء ومعناه التوسعة

TABRISI:73:1-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:1-10/r9.claim: The verb sabbakha means spreading cotton for carding; al-Akhṭal's cited line compares scattered dust to carded cotton.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r9.anchor: يقال: سبخت القطن إذا وسعته للندف

TABRISI:73:1-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:73:1-10/r10.claim: The Prophet told ʿĀʾisha, who was praying against a thief, not to lighten or relieve her curse by supplication.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r10.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة

TABRISI:73:1-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r11.speaker: ثعلب
TABRISI:73:1-10/r11.claim: Thaʿlab says sabḥ means restless movement and agitation, while sabkh means stillness.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r11.anchor: وقال ثعلب: السبح التردد والاضطراب والسبخ السكون

TABRISI:73:1-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:1-10/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:73:1-10/r12.claim: A Prophetic saying describes fever as heat from Hell and says to calm it with water.
TABRISI:73:1-10/r12.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:73:8-9/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:73:8-9/r8.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet has the day for going about and attending to his needs.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r8.anchor: معناه أن لك يا محمد في النهار منصرفا ومنقلبا إلى ما تقضي فيه حوائجك عن قتادة

TABRISI:73:8-9/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r9.claim: The Prophet's daytime duties include conveying the message, calling people, teaching obligations and practices, and providing for his family; night frees the heart for remembrance and recitation.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r9.anchor: فإنك تحتاج فيه إلى تبليغ الرسالة ودعوة الخلق وتعليم الفرائض والسنن وإصلاح المعيشة

TABRISI:73:8-9/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:73:8-9/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:73:8-9/r10.claim: Teaching and learning do not excuse neglecting night prayer: the Prophet had greater teaching demands yet did not forgo his share.
TABRISI:73:8-9/r10.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا عذر لأحد في ترك صلاة الليل لأجل التعليم والتعلم

FARRA:v3p196#2/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p196#2/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p196#2/r10.claim: The long daytime activity is time to take care of one’s needs.
FARRA:v3p196#2/r10.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا (7) . يقول: لك في النهار ما يقضي حوائجك.

FARRA:v3p196#2/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p196#2/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p196#2/r11.claim: Some read سبخا with khāʾ; tasbīkh means loosening or spreading wool and cotton, as in the command “spread your cotton.”
FARRA:v3p196#2/r11.anchor: وقد قرأ بعضهم : «سبخا» بالخاء، والتسبيخ: توسعة الصوف والقطن وما أشبهه، يقال: سبخي قطنك.

FARRA:v3p196#2/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p196#2/r12.speaker: أبو زياد الكلابي
FARRA:v3p196#2/r12.claim: Abu Ziyad al-Kilabi told al-Farra that Bedouins say “God, ease it from him” for a sick or stung person, illustrating سبخ.
FARRA:v3p196#2/r12.anchor: حضر أبو زياد الكلابي مجلس الفراء فى هذا اليوم، فسأله الفراء عن هذا الحرف فقال: أهل باديتنا يقولون: اللهم سبخ عنه للمريض والملسوع ونحوه.

THALABI:v10p62/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
THALABI:v10p62/r1.claim: The common reading has sabḥ with ḥāʾ; it means free time and latitude for sleep and needs, from the basic sense of moving quickly.
THALABI:v10p62/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: بالحاء غير معجمة، أي فراغا وسعة لنومك وتصرفك في حوائجك

THALABI:v10p62/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p62/r2.claim: The root also appears in swimming and in describing a fast-running horse as sābiḥ; an unnamed poet uses sabḥ for broad movement.
THALABI:v10p62/r2.anchor: وأصل السبح سرعة الذهاب. ومنه السباحة في الماء، وفرس سابح شديد الجري

THALABI:v10p62/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62/r3.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
THALABI:v10p62/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar reads sabkhan with khāʾ, meaning ease, latitude, and respite; the Prophet’s phrase to ʿĀʾisha uses the verb to mean lighten.
THALABI:v10p62/r3.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر: سبخا بالخاء المعجمة، أراد خفة وسعة واستراحة

THALABI:v10p62/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p62/r4.claim: Tasbīkh means loosening and fluffing cotton or wool; al-Akhṭal compares dogs scattering dust to loose cotton fibers.
THALABI:v10p62/r4.anchor: والتسبيخ توسيع القطن والصوف وتنفيشها، يقال للمرأة: سبخي قطنك

THALABI:v10p62/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p62/r5.speaker: تغلب
THALABI:v10p62/r5.claim: Taghlib contrasts sabḥ, movement and agitation, with sabkh, stillness; a prophetic saying about cooling fever with water illustrates sabkh as calming.
THALABI:v10p62/r5.anchor: قال تغلب: السبح التردد والاضطراب والسبخ السكون ومنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r1.claim: For the preceding daytime activity, Ibn al-Aʿrābī gives the senses of movement and livelihood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r1.anchor: قال (¬9) ابن الأعرابي: معناه اضطرابا ومعاشا (¬10).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r2.claim: Al-Layth glosses the preceding phrase as leisure for the moon.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r3.claim: Daytime gives room for sleep and attending to needs, leaving the night for prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p364#3/r3.anchor: أنه يفرغ في النهار للنوم، والتصرف في الحوائج فيكون ليله للصلاة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494/r1.claim: Sabḥ means activity in one's needs, coming and going, and traveling back and forth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p494/r1.anchor: أي تصرفا في حوائجك، وإقبالا وإدبارا، [وذهابا ومجيئا]

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r6.claim: Daytime is long activity in one's needs, coming and going; this urges night prayer and Quran recitation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:73:4-8/r6.anchor: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا } أي: تصرفا في حوائجك إقبالا وإدبارا، وهذا حث على القيام بالليل لقراءة القرآن.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p215/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p215/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p215/r5.claim: The long daytime activity means going about, coming and going for one’s needs and occupations.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p215/r5.anchor: وقوله: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا (7) [المزمل: 7] يعني: تصرفا وإقبالا وإدبارا في حوائجك وأشغالك.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r5.claim: Besides swimming, sabḥ is metaphorically explained as rushing about among needs and activities, making journeys, or moving around; the translation adopts this sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r5.anchor: 7. âyetteki sebh kelimesi, “yüzme” anlamının yanında, mecaz olarak, “ihtiyaçlar ve türlü meşguliyet alanları için koşuşturma, gidip gelme, dolaşıp durma” şeklinde de açıklanmış olup (bk. Şevkânî, V, 366) meâlde bu mâna dikkate alınmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r6.claim: The Prophet and, by extension, his community will spend the day earning a livelihood, conveying the Qur'an, teaching religion, and handling other tasks, so night suits worship better.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:73:5/r6.anchor: gündüzleri daha çok maişet temini, Kur’an’ı tebliğ, dini öğretme ve daha başka işlerle meşgul olacakları, bu tür maksatlarla koşuşturacakları; bu sebeple namaz, Kur’an okuma gibi ibadetler için gecenin daha uygun bir zaman olduğu hatırlatılmıştır.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r1.claim: Ali b. Ubayd Allah says sabḥ originally means running; tasbīḥ is running in God's glorification through magnifying and declaring Him free of fault.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : السبح : أصله الجري . يقال : سبح يسبح سبحا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris defines tasbīḥ as declaring God exalted above every evil.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : التسبيح : تنزيه الله تعالى من كل سوء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r3.claim: The related words sabāḥa and sabḥa mean swimming and prayer, while sabḥ can mean free time.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r3.anchor: والسباحة : العوم . والسبحة : الصلاة : والسبح : الفراغ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r4.claim: One Qur'anic sense is free time; the verse says the day contains a long span of it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r4.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السبح في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r5.claim: A second sense is movement or orbiting, as celestial bodies move in their courses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السبح في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r6.claim: A third sense is ships sailing through the sea.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p347/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السبح في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

DAMGHANI:v1p227/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p227/r1.claim: Sabḥ can mean free time or leisure during the day.
DAMGHANI:v1p227/r1.anchor: فوجه منها : السبح الفراغ قوله تعالى في سورة المزمل
